title: Multi-Level Cache System
description: Build a multi-level caching system with LRU eviction, TTL support, and write strategies.

steps.title: Implement LRU Cache Data Structure
steps.description: Create an `LRUCache` class using a doubly-linked list and a hashmap. The cache should have `get(key)` and `put(key, value)` methods. On `put`, if the key exists, move it to the front. If the cache exceeds capacity, evict the least recently used item. Print the evicted keys when they are removed.
hints: Use a Map for O(1) lookups combined with a doubly-linked list for ordering
Track head and tail pointers; move accessed nodes to head
When evicting, remove the tail node and delete it from the Map

verification.successMessage: LRU cache correctly evicts least recently used items
verification.failureMessage: LRU cache did not evict the expected keys

steps.title: Add TTL (Time-To-Live) Support
steps.description: Extend the `LRUCache` to support per-key TTL. Each entry stores an expiration timestamp. On `get()`, check if the entry has expired; if so, remove it and print `'Expired: key'`. Accept an optional `ttlMs` parameter in the constructor (default 0 = no expiry).
hints: Store `expiresAt` timestamp alongside value and list node
Use `Date.now()` to compare against expiration on every get
Evict expired items during get (lazy expiration) to avoid a sweep timer

verification.successMessage: TTL expiry correctly detected and reported
verification.failureMessage: Expired key was not detected on access

steps.title: Implement Write-Through Strategy
steps.description: Create a `WriteThroughCache` that wraps the LRU cache. On `put(key, value)`, write to both the cache and a backing store (simulated as an array of `{key, value}` objects). Print `'Cache: key=value'` and `'Store: key=value'` on each write. On `get(key)`, read from cache first, then fall back to the store.
hints: The backing store can be a simple array that you push entries into
On write, always update both cache and store before returning
On read miss in cache, check the store and populate the cache

verification.successMessage: Write-through correctly writes to both cache and store
verification.failureMessage: Write-through did not write to both layers

steps.title: Implement Write-Behind Strategy
steps.description: Create a `WriteBehindCache` that batches writes and flushes them asynchronously. Accumulate `put()` calls into a batch queue. On flush (triggered manually or after N items), write the batch to the backing store and print `'Flushed: [key1, key2, ...]'`. Print `'Queued: key'` when a write is added to the batch.
hints: Maintain a Set or Map of dirty keys and their values
Use `setTimeout(fn, 0)` or a manual `flush()` method to simulate async
Clear the batch after flushing to avoid duplicate writes

verification.successMessage: Write-behind correctly batches and flushes writes
verification.failureMessage: Write-behind did not batch or flush properly

steps.title: Build Multi-Level Cache (L1/L2)
steps.description: Create a `MultiLevelCache` with an L1 (fast, small, LRU with 2-item capacity) and L2 (slow, large, LRU with 10-item capacity) cache. On `get(key)`, check L1 first, then L2. On a miss in L1 but hit in L2, promote the item to L1. Print `'L1 hit: key'`, `'L2 hit: key'`, or `'Miss: key'` for each access.
hints: Compose your existing LRUCache class — pass different capacities
On L2 hit, put the item into L1 so future accesses are fast
On L1 eviction, the item is still in L2 so no data is lost

verification.successMessage: Multi-level cache correctly cascades lookups between L1 and L2
verification.failureMessage: Multi-level cache did not cascade correctly

steps.title: Add Cache Statistics
steps.description: Add instrumentation to the `MultiLevelCache` that tracks `hits`, `misses`, and `evictions` per level. Expose a `stats()` method returning a report. After a series of operations, print the stats object showing hit count, miss count, and eviction count for each level.
hints: Increment counters on every get/put path — hits++, misses++, evictions++
Store stats per level in a map or separate objects
Print `JSON.stringify(stats)` for a clean formatted report

verification.successMessage: Statistics are correctly tracked and printed
verification.failureMessage: Statistics output is missing expected fields
